tossups.text: This author has written short story collections like The Elephant Vanishes and after the quake, as well as the novel Wild Sheep Chase. One of his works concerns Watanabe Toru in 1960s Japan. In addition to Norwegian Wood, this author wrote about the intertwined fates of Tamura and Nakata, as well as a man who searches for his wife and cat in a magical underworld of Tokyo, Okada Toru. Name this Japanese author of Kafka on the Shore and The Wind-Up Bird Chronicle.

The largest one of these events in the United States occurred in 1910 in Kern County, California at Lakeview Gusher. During the First Gulf War, Saddam Hussein claimed that American attacks on two ships had caused one of these events. A more famous one of these events occurred in Prince William Sound in 1989 when a merchant vessel ran aground on a reef; long-term effects from that incident continue to affect Alaska. An explosion on the Deepwater Horizon platform resulted in, For 10 points, what type of disaster that describes environmental contamination from the release of liquid petroleum?

This city's fortress of Sacsayhuamán ["sawk-say-wah-MAHN"] was constructed by the Killke ["KEY-ke"] culture. Conflict over the jurisdiction over this city resulted in the Battle of Las Salinas, after which Diego de Almagro was executed. This city, built in the shape of the sacred puma, had its Coricancha temple stripped of gold in order to pay a ransom for its ruler. After leading resistance from Vilcabamba, Túpac Amaru was executed in this city. During a civil war, Huáscar was captured defending this city from the forces of Atahualpa, who had been imprisoned by Francisco Pizarro. For 10 points, name this capital of the Inca Empire.

Unlike other regions in the ventral striatum, the islands of Calleja ("cah-yay-ha") exhibit no expression of this compound's second receptor. Sinemet, which includes a precursor to this compound, is used with entacapone to treat end-of-dose "wearing-off" symptoms by inhibiting this compound's breakdown by AADC and COMT. MPTP destroys neurons of the pars compacta that release this compound, causing permanent symptoms of Parkinson's disease. Adrenaline is synthesized through the sequential hydroxylation and methylation of this compound, and this catecholamine ("cat-uh-ko-la-meen") is itself produced from the decarboxylation of levodopa. For 10 points, name this neurotransmitter that is associated with pleasure and reward-motivated behavior.

The Seminoles fought two wars to prevent being forced into this event. Andrew Jackson ignored a Supreme Court order protecting the Cherokee from this event. For 10 points, name this event in which Cherokee, Chickasaw, Choctaw, and Creek tribes were led away from their lands in the Southeast United States.

this structure is essential for cranial nerves. It plays a key role in the nervous system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this cranial nerve-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The cranial nerve is a key component of the Nervous system, involved in cranial nerves.

tossups.text: Stephen Kleene introduced a thesis named for this scientist and an advisor that equates classes of computable functions. The busy beaver problem seeks to maximize the output of constructs named for this scientist, which include a set of transition functions, accepting states, and a head. Like Alonzo Church's lambda calculus, any algorithm can be encoded on an infinite tape known as this scientist's namesake "machines." This scientist proposed a namesake test that he called the "imitation game" to distinguish between humans and artificial intelligence. For 10 points, name this British mathematician who cracked the Enigma code.

this structure is essential for cortisol functions. It plays a key role in the endocrine system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this adrenal-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The adrenal is a key component of the Endocrine system, involved in cortisol functions.

tossups.text: One of this author's characters writes a poem about a glow-worm who is resentful of the fairies who depend on him to provide light for their parties. This author wrote two of the three novels that are analyzed in Eve Kosofsky Sedgwick's essay "The Character in the Veil." In the frame story of one novel by this author, an Englishman asks a priest why a certain assassin is being sheltered in a Neapolitan church. The protagonist notices an uncanny resemblance between a nun at the convent of St. Clair and a miniature portrait found among her father's belongings in another novel by this author, who was nicknamed "The Great Enchantress." The villainous priest Father Schedoni attempts to prevent Ellena Rosalba and Vincentio di Vivaldi from marrying each other in this author's novel The Italian. In her most famous novel, Signor Montoni keeps Emily St. Aubert captive in the title Italian castle. For 10 points, name this author of the Gothic novel The Mysteries of Udolpho.

The PI curve graphs the performance of this process, rising as you move along the x-axis until a namesake "reaction center" is damaged in "inhibition" caused by high intensity. Malic acid is stored in vacuoles as part of one form of this larger process, while in another form of this larger process oxalo•acetate is released in bundle sheath cells after it is formed in mesophyll cells. In the most common form of this process, NADP+ is reduced to NADPH, and it takes place across the thylakoid membrane of chloroplast organelles. CAM, C4, and the Calvin Cycle are alternate forms of, for 10 points, what process, in which ATP is produced from sunlight?

With the help of Princess Marie Bonaparte, this man escaped Austria after his books were burned by the Nazis and his daughter Anna was interrogated by the Gestapo. As part of his earlier medical research, he wrote a paper titled, "On Coca" advocating the use of cocaine. This man is best known for works such as Totem and Taboo , Beyond the Pleasure Principle , and The Ego and the Id. For ten points, name this Austrian neurologist who developed psychoanalysis.

In human anatomy, this structure is essential for neuron structure. It plays a key role in the nervous system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this axon-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The axon is a key component of the Nervous system, involved in neuron structure.

tossups.text: The "Three Pagodas Pass" in this country lies near this country's Isan region. In the middle of this country is the prominent Khorat Plateau, and its largest Northern city is Chiang Mai. This country's capital lies on the Chao Phraya River, which flows into this country's namesake gulf, an arm of the South China Sea. This country shares the Kra Isthmus, part of the Malay peninsula, with its neighbor Burma. For ten points, name this Southeast Asian country formerly known as Siam with its capital at Bangkok.

One episode in this novel shows a washerwoman screaming while clutched by another character, while she later is seized and carried away by a student. Another character appears in her nightgown and explains that she has a businessman locked up in a small room. The protagonist of this novel is confused to see a person in Fraulein Burstner's room, and he later buys three paintings from Titorelli in exchange for advice. Leni is the assistant to the lawyer Hull in this novel, who is engaged by the protagonist but only considers drafting a petition. This novel concludes when the protagonist is taken to a quarry and executed on his 31st birthday. For 10 points, name this novel about the arrest and persecution of a bank manager named Joseph K, written by Franz Kafka.

In Norse myth, Eggther owns one of these items, which he uses mournfully during Ragnarok instead of participating. In Shinto, one of these objects is used in a form of divination called Koto-ura. In Irish myth, the Dagda recovered one of these items from a Formorian camp, which he always took into battle and used to manipulate emotions. Amphion used one of these items in the construction of Thebes, and another one of them was exchanged for some cattle by one god. Also used to combat the Sirens during the quest for the Golden Fleece, the first one was created from a tortoise shell by Hermes, and one of them was used in a failed recovery of Eurydice. For 10 points, name these stringed instruments used by Orpheus and Apollo.

This man's namesake particle is a black hole with a Schwarzchild radius close to its Compton wavelength, while his namesake unit of time is equal to 5.39 times 10 to the -40 seconds. A series of equations used to describe Brownian motion are named for this man and Fokker. One equation named for him, whose peak can be found by Wien's [veenz] law, resolved the ultraviolet catastrophe by correcting the Rayleigh-Jeans law. His namesake postulate states that the energy of a photon equals h times frequency, which he discovered while working with blackbodies. For 10 points, name this man who postulated that energy is quantized and comes in multiples of his namesake constant.

This leader encouraged citizens to voice their opinions during the Hundred Flowers Campaign. This man's wife was part of the "Gang of Four", and he gave mangoes to workers who quelled factioning "Red Guards" during the Cultural Revolution. This author of the "Little Red Book" led forces during the Long March, and tried to improve his country in his Great Leap Forward. For 10 points, name this first communist leader of China.

This text notes that "it is altogether fitting and proper" that a cemetery should be dedicated, but that the land has already been consecrated by those who "gave the last full measure of devotion." This two-minute speech ends by resolving that "government of the people, by the people, for the people, shall not perish from the earth." For 10 points, name this speech written by Abraham Lincoln "four score and seven years" after American independence.

The narrator of one of this author's stories ponders a word he compares to "gnomon in the Euclid" or "simony in the Catechism" upon hearing of another character's death. Father Purdon's sermon comparing sins to verifying accounts ends that story by this author, in which Mr. Kernan is taken to a retreat upon tripping down the stairs drunk. The death of a character created by this author who frequents, the vaguely-named store Drapery, causes the narrator to contemplate the word "paralysis." The Morkan sisters invite Bartell D'Arcy to perform at the central event of another story by this author. In that story by this author, the song "The Lass of Aughrim" was sung by Michael Furey when courting the wife of Gabriel Conroy. For 10 points, name this author, who included "Grace," "The Sisters," and "The Dead" in Dubliners.

Moderator note: Read musical notes slowly Antonio Vivaldi likely wrote the first solo concerto for this instrument and wrote 39 of them total. It's not the clarinet, but this instrument's two most-played concerti are von Weber's in F major and Mozart's in B-flat major, both the only ones by their composers. Upon hearing one solo on this instrument, which begins "long C, B C B, G E B A," Camille Saint-Saens said that if he was hearing one of them, he was a monkey; that high solo opens Stravinsky's Rite of Spring. In Prokofiev's Peter and the Wolf, this low instrument represents the grandfather. For 10 points, name this double-reed instrument, which with its "contra" variety are the lowest woodwinds in the orchestra.

parts.text: Name this epic poem, in which a sailor retells his experiences to the Wedding-Guest after shooting an albatross.
parts.answer: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner
acceptableAnswers: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner

parts.text: The Rime of The Ancient Mariner is by this Fireside Poet, who wrote that "My genial spirits fall" in "Dejection: An Ode."
In this Coleridge poem, the title character decrees a "stately pleasure-dome" where "Alph, the sacred river, ran".

bonuses.leadin: The narrator of this poem claims that there is "water, water everywhere, nor any drop to drink". For 10 points each:

parts.text: This 1763 rebellion led by a namesake Ottawa chieftain, fought by the first significant multi-nation alliance, resulted in a stalemate. It included the use of smallpox blankets in the siege of Fort Pitt.

This nation and the Mingo fought in Lord Dunmore's War under Cornstalk, and its chief Blue Jacket led the native forces at Fallen Timbers with the Miami Little Turtle. Tecumseh was a later leader of this nation.

Teedyuscung was forced to give up this nation's land in eastern Pennsylvania after the French and Indian War. This nation shares a name with the river flowing through Philadelphia, also the name of the colony east of Maryland.

bonuses.leadin: Name the following about 18th century Native American wars, for 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this politician known as the Kingfish, who was the basis for Willie Stark in the novel All the King's Men.
Huey Long promoted this program of money redistribution during his tenure in the U.S. Senate, which he claimed would provide five thousand dollars for every poor family.
This anti-Semitic minister and friend of Huey Long co-led the Share Our Wealth movement. He was also involved with William Pelley's fascist Silver Shirts.

bonuses.leadin: While governor of Louisiana, he created the Bureau of Criminal Identification, a police force that reported directly to him and could make arrests without warrants. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this statement which causes the standard deviation of position times the standard deviation of momentum to be greater than h-bar over two.
Heisenberg was a student and rival of this Jewish Danish physicist, who formulated a model of the atom backed by Rydberg's formula involving orbits.

The actual commutator of position and momentum is h-bar times this number. This number multiplies reactance in the formula for impedance, and it also multiplies h-bar in the time-dependent Schrodinger equation.
acceptableAnswers: the square root of negative one

bonuses.leadin: This statement only applies if two operators, when applied to each other, do not give the same answer when applied in the reverse order. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this 18th century Empress of Russia, an "enlightened despot" who supported the works of Voltaire and Diderot while brutally crushing uprisings like Pugachev's Rebellion.
Catherine fought two successful wars against this empire in modern-day Turkey. This "sick man of Europe" dissolved after World War I.
Catherine also attempted to open trade with Edo-era Japan. At the time, Japan was ruled by this government, which lasted until the Meiji Restoration in 1868.

bonuses.leadin: This leader may have had her husband, Peter III, killed, so that she could take the throne. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with types of joints.
What is the main function of the synovial in the musculoskeletal system?
Name another component of the musculoskeletal system related to types of joints.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human musculoskeletal system.

parts.text: It is the change of a certain state function with respect to the number of molecules. That state function is frequently internal energy, Gibbs free energy, or enthalpy.
In the quantum mechanical version of an ideal gas, the chemical potential at absolute zero is called this man's energy.
This quantity can be used to make the chemical potential equation for a real gas resemble that for an ideal gas. It measures the tendency for a substance to change to a different phase.

bonuses.leadin: Answer some questions about a thermodynamic quantity, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with major veins (vena cava, jugular, portal).
What is the main function of the aorta in the cardiovascular system?
Name another component of the cardiovascular system related to major veins (vena cava, jugular, portal).

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human cardiovascular system.

parts.text: Name this 1972 novel about the titular artist who studies under Jacob Kahn before conveying his mother Rivkeh's pain in his masterpiece Brooklyn Crucifixion.
acceptableAnswers: The My Name is Asher Lev

parts.text: This Jewish author of My Name is Asher Lev wrote about the friendship of the Jewish teenagers Reuven Malter and Daniel Saunders in his first novel The Chosen.
The title character of this Potok novel is the young Polish immigrant Ilana who helps her mother Anne Chandal break her allegiance to the Communist party and return to the Jewish faith.

bonuses.leadin: The protagonist refuses to move to Vienna with his father despite being ordered to do so by a religious leader called "The Rebbe." For 10 points:

parts.text: Sucrose is a disaccharide formed by an alpha-1,2-glycosidic linkage between glucose and this molecule. This monosaccharide can be incorporated into glycolysis at an intermediate step involving a phosphate bound to this molecule.
This enzyme catalyzes the rate determining step of the investment phase of glycolysis. It forms fructose-1,6-bisphosphate from fructose-6-phosphate and ATP.

This compound has the highest-energy phosphate bond formed in living organisms. It is formed from the action of enolase on 2-phosphoglycerate in glycolysis, and by the decarboxylation of oxaloacetate in gluconeogenesis.

bonuses.leadin: A common sweetener is formed by processing corn syrup in order to enrich it in this molecule. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this class of drugs that includes psilocybin and LSD. Today, these drugs are being researched for their potential use in treating depression.
In addition to depression, psychedelic drugs may also help treat this disorder that might be caused by exposure to highly shocking or hurtful events, such as abuse, assault, or war.
Another focus of psychedelic research is the treatment of the "cluster" type of this common ailment. A severe form of this ailment is called a migraine.

bonuses.leadin: Abraham Maslow believed that fully self-actualized people underwent feelings of harmony called "peak experiences," which could be induced with these substances. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with bone development and growth.
What is the main function of the skull in the musculoskeletal system?
Name another component of the musculoskeletal system related to bone development and growth.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human musculoskeletal system.

parts.text: The Timewheel is a scaled-up one of these devices, but instead of taking 60 minutes, it takes a year for sand to fall from the upper chamber to the lower chamber.

The Timewheel is located at the former site of a statue of Lenin that was moved to this city's Memento Park. Witness Square in this city holds a replica of just Stalin's boots, as the rest of his body was pulled down.
The Timewheel was built to commemorate Hungary taking this action in 2004. The Treaty of Maastricht partly defines the criteria needed to take this action.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about the Timewheel. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these creatures that can decide, as fetuses, whether they want to be born or not, and who eat the flesh of the unemployed. Their utopian society is visited by a psychiatric patient in a namesake 1927 novel.
In this story by the author of Kappa, the criminal Kandata shows compassion to the title animal, but screws up the chance given to him to escape Hell using the title object produced by that animal.
This Japanese author wrote Kappa and "The Spider's Thread," but is better known for the stories "In a Grove" and "Rashomon."

bonuses.leadin: The "Viverist" religion of these creatures teaches them that they are descended from the Tree of Life. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this beautiful mortal man and lover of Aphrodite. Aphrodite asks him not to go out to hunt, but he does anyway and is killed by a wild boar.
Adonis was born out of a tree that used to be this woman. This woman was transformed into a tree as punishment for having sex with her father, King Cinyras ("sin-NYE-russ").

In the Metamorphoses, the story of Adonis is framed as a song sung by this musician. This hero travels to the underworld to bring back his wife Eurydice ("yoo-RID-uh-see"), but he fails since he turns back to look at her.

bonuses.leadin: This character's name derives from a Canaanite word for "Lord," which has the same root as a Hebrew word that may substitute for the name Yahweh ("YAH-way") when speaking aloud. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these substances whose namesake constant is abbreviated R and has a value of 8.314 Joules per Kelvin per mol.
In the Van Der Waals modification of the Ideal Gas Law, the coefficient "a" corrects this quantity by accounting for any intermolecular forces.

A molecule in an ideal gas has a kinetic energy of 3/2 times Boltzmann's constant times temperature as a result of this theorem. This theorem relates the distribution of the energy of a system to its degrees of freedom.

bonuses.leadin: For these substances, the fugacity coefficient and compressibility factor are equal to 1. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Aaron Burr defeated Philip Schuyler to become a senator from this state. The Rensselaer family owned a substantial amount of land in this state.
Burr was the first grand sachem (SAY-kuhm) of this New York City political machine. Cartoons by Thomas Nast depicted this organization as a tiger.
In his later life, Aaron Burr was involved in a bizarre plan to establish himself as the hereditary emperor of this country, America's southern neighbor.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about Aaron Burr, (sir), for 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this British rock band who also sang "You Can't Always Get What You Want."
The Rolling Stones' lead singer is this musician, known for his dance moves and facial expressions.
Jagger's dance moves are honored in the song "Moves Like Jagger" by this American band.

bonuses.leadin: This band had hits with the songs "Jumpin' Jack Flash" and "Satisfaction." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this American Transcendentalist, who gave a notable address to the Harvard Divinity School in addition to authoring essays such as The Over-Soul and Self-Reliance.
This Emerson speech preceded the Harvard Divinity School address and was given to the Phi Beta Kappa society at Cambridge. It argued for a break from European cultural tradition.
In his essay Nature, Emerson discussed the need to observe nature in solitude, and describes how he becomes a transparent one of these objects, saying that "I am nothing; I see all."

bonuses.leadin: This thinker quipped that "a foolish consistency is the hobgoblin of little minds." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this genre consisting of a libretto text set to music.
This Italian composer is credited along with librettist Alessandro Striggio with creating the earliest opera that is still regularly performed, L'Orfeo.
Monteverdi premiered L'Orfeo in this city in northern Italy for the Gonzaga family. It is also where Romeo is banished to in Romeo and Juliet.

bonuses.leadin: The first work of this type, Dafne, has no existing copies, but one could hear different works of this type at La Scala in Milan. For 10 points each:
